problem: Expose the coordinator adapter as a qrexec process boundary without turning stdin/stdout into an unbounded parser, leaking secrets on failures, or adding a long-lived daemon before transport contracts are proven.

independentReviews.winner: single JSON envelope per process with strict byte limits and one attested JSON response
independentReviews.why: Matches qrexec process-per-call semantics, avoids stream framing ambiguity, and keeps request identity bound to the existing authenticated envelope and attested response.
rejected: newline-delimited multi-request process because one process could accumulate cross-request state and framing ambiguity
unbounded stdin buffering because a peer could force memory growth before authentication

independentReviews.winner: fixed non-diagnostic stderr on transport/auth/config failures; authenticated coordinator outcomes stay on attested stdout
independentReviews.why: Prevents request bodies, HMACs, lease tokens, filesystem paths, private-key material, and stack traces from being reflected through qrexec error channels.
rejected: raw exception messages and stacks on stderr because they can become an information-disclosure surface
silently truncating oversized input/output because it can create ambiguous protocol state

independentReviews.winner: thin process wrapper around the existing adapter
independentReviews.why: Adds no qrexec round trip, daemon, database, watcher, or persistent process; the only added work is bounded JSON parsing/serialization and environment validation.
rejected: long-lived transport daemon because it adds lifecycle, memory, replay-cache, and crash-recovery state
extra preflight/attestation RPC because it adds latency without improving the existing request-bound signature contract

required: spawned process accepts exactly one authenticated JSON envelope and emits exactly one request-bound Ed25519-attested response
oversized input fails closed with empty stdout
response size is bounded before stdout write
failure stderr is constant and contains no request secret, transport secret, private key, or lease token
qa.knownGap: Process-death fault injection around the adapter mutation/journal boundary remains covered at adapter level; the next QA step should exercise the same crash points through the spawned service process without exposing a production fault-injection switch.

safety: Synthetic/defensive lab transport only. No real financial transactions, stolen payment data, fraud workflows, or weakened security controls.
